reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) discusses tungsten refractory HEAs and plasma-facing materials but provides no data on WC-reinforced HEA composites, tribological behavior, or tribolayer formation. None of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: WC particles can be uniformly dispersed in a HEA matrix via powder metallurgy or laser cladding
Dispersed WC particles act as hard barriers reducing plastic deformation and adhesion during sliding
WC promotes formation of a continuous, lubricious, and protective tribolayer containing WC fragments and oxidized HEA phases
This tribolayer reduces friction and wear across a wide temperature range (RT to ~800 °C)
The composite will show ~60–70% reduction in friction and wear versus the untreated HEA
